name: RECODE
full_name: REactor neutrino COherent scattering Detection Experiment
summary: RECODE is a high-purity germanium programme at the Sanmen reactor laboratory designed to measure coherent reactor-antineutrino scattering. Multiple detector locations and low ionization thresholds are intended to test background and distance dependence.
detection_principle: Point-contact germanium detectors measure low-energy ionization from nuclear recoils. Active/passive shielding and reactor-correlated comparisons isolate the signal; planned arrays at different distances provide complementary flux and systematic checks.

sites.name: China; Sanmen nuclear power plant, Zhejiang
sites.location: China; Sanmen nuclear power plant, Zhejiang

status.label: Detector site tests / preparing physics deployment
status.evidence: The July 2026 collaboration report describes completed tests at 65 m from the core. Safety confirmation for the intended 11 m and 22 m sites was still in progress, with physics running projected for late 2026.

timeline.event: Sanmen continuation of the reactor-scattering programme documented
Detector stability and acquisition tests performed at the 65 m reactor site

key_parameters.name: Completed site tests
key_parameters.value: Three Ge detectors at 65 m from the core; more than 50 days of stable operation for each

key_parameters.name: Intended physics baselines
key_parameters.value: 11 m near and 22 m far; deployment still prospective in July 2026

key_parameters.name: Demonstrated test analysis threshold
key_parameters.value: 250 eV electron equivalent; lower than 200 eV remained an upgrade goal

phases.name: Sanmen detector tests
phases.description: Three detectors operated in a container at 65 m from the core.

phases.name: Near/far physics programme
phases.description: 11 m and 22 m sites were undergoing safety confirmation in the July 2026 report; late-2026 running was a projection.

results.summary: The collaboration demonstrated stable detector/site-test performance and background analysis. This should not be confused with a completed CEvNS measurement at the intended near/far baselines.
